request.deadline: 12 months after deployment; month-6 yield distribution; audit expected by July 1, 2026
deliverables: Deploy treasury-owned capital into Strike Finance V2 USDM liquidity infrastructure for 12 months.
Return realized yield from the first six months to the Cardano Treasury at month 6.
Return 100% of remaining treasury-owned deployed assets, including principal and remaining realized yield, at month 12 subject to realized losses.

Provide monthly public transparency reports covering deployment status, liquidity utilization, volume, open interest, P&L, yield, drawdown, stablecoin exposure, market quality metrics, distributions, and material risks.
Publish third-party assurance reports for deployment confirmation, month-6 yield distribution, and month-12 return of funds.
request.recipient: Independent multisig council composed of Rami from Snek, Phil from Surf, and James from Monetra/Moneta as administrator; Strike Finance is the project benefiting from deployed liquidity.
request.what: 12-month productive treasury deployment into Strike Finance V2 liquidity infrastructure, with ADA sold for USDM to provide stablecoin-denominated liquidity.

claims.claim: The proposal requests 9,000,000 ADA for a 12-month liquidity deployment into Strike Finance V2 rather than grant funding.
The deployed ADA will be sold for USDM, modeled at ADA = 0.15 USD to create approximately 1,350,000 USDM of stablecoin liquidity.
Under modeled assumptions of a 10% USD-denominated APR, the deployment is expected to generate about 135,000 USD or 900,000 ADA-equivalent in annual yield, but returns are not guaranteed.

Strike reports more than 1.13 billion USD in cumulative trading volume, around 968,000 to 1,001,000 trades, over 3,000 unique traders, over 1.16 million USD in protocol revenue, and over 3.25 million USD in liquidity provider profit.
Strike V2 public data from 2026-03-20 through 2026-06-15 is presented as evidence of growth in volume, trades, users, revenue, open interest, and liquidity vault TVL.

The proposal asserts that liquidity depth is the primary bottleneck to Strike's further growth and that added stablecoin liquidity can improve execution, trader retention, volume, yield, and Cardano-native DeFi activity.
Operational custody is proposed through an independent multisig council, and Strike Finance is stated not to have unilateral custody or control of treasury assets.

The proposal identifies risks including ADA price appreciation opportunity cost, USDM depeg or redemption risk, smart contract risk, yield underperformance, liquidity risk, and multisig operational risk.

Governance review is triggered if drawdown exceeds 8%, reporting is missed for two consecutive monthly cycles, or unresolved custody, accounting, stablecoin, redemption, or smart contract concerns arise, with mandatory review at 10% drawdown and a separate wind-down review trigger above 20% drawdown.

The proposal states that Strike V2 is live on mainnet, has had unofficial reviews, and is undergoing an official audit by Christian Schmitz expected to be finalized by July 1, 2026, with publication upon completion.

summary: The document describes a 9,000,000 ADA, 12-month treasury-owned liquidity deployment into Strike Finance V2 using USDM, with modeled yield, multisig custody, reporting, assurance, risk triggers, and return of funds, but many performance and feasibility assertions are presented without embedded references.
